intro: Jobs similar to dermatologists are mostly other physician specialties. By O*NET 31.0 data, the closest are Allergists and Immunologists (86% similar), General Internal Medicine Physicians (84%) and Optometrists (84%). 19 of the 20 similar careers are in the same broad field.
shared: These careers share long patient visits, careful examination and steady follow-up care. O*NET rates service orientation at 4 out of 5 for dermatologists and social perceptiveness at 3.88. That patient focus is why allergy, internal medicine, neurology and rehabilitation medicine come out close. Nearly all of them need a medical degree and residency, and only one pays more than the $328,730 dermatologist median.

faq.q: Which jobs like dermatologist pay more?
faq.a: Only 1 of the 20 similar careers pays more: Emergency Medicine Physicians earn a BLS May 2025 median of $335,550, which is 2% more than dermatologists. General internists earn $256,560, about 22% less, and Neurologists earn $248,560, about 24% less.

faq.q: Are there jobs like dermatologist that need less training?
faq.a: Few. Only 1 of the 20 similar careers usually needs less preparation: Exercise Physiologists. Optometrists are 84% similar and need a doctor of optometry degree rather than medical school, but they earn $136,570, which is 58% less than dermatologists, so the shorter path comes with a large pay cut.
